CM Mohan Yadav's international investment roadshows (UK & Germany tour, Japan visit, Barcelona/Spain visit, Dubai/UAE visits) that produced bilateral company MoUs feeding into GIS 2025 and subsequent conclaves

method: WebSearch (~25 queries before the session's WebSearch budget was exhausted partway through, then again available later in the session) to identify candidate MoUs from GIS 2025, MP Tech Growth Conclave 3.0, regional conclaves, and CM international roadshows, cross-checked against Invest MP's own event pages. When WebSearch and both DuckDuckGo-via-curl and Bing-via-curl scraping were blocked/rate-limited mid-session, pivoted to Google News RSS feeds (news.google.com/rss/search) fetched via curl to discover article titles/sources, then resolved actual article content either directly via WebFetch (for sites that allow it) or via the r.jina.ai reader proxy (for sites WebFetch could not reach directly, e.g. DataCenterDynamics). Every company included below was verified by opening and reading at least one substantive source directly - not from a search snippet alone - and cross-referenced against a second independent outlet where possible. Companies that appeared only in a single unverifiable press release, that could not be confirmed as foreign-headquartered, or that were flagged by other sources as low-credibility were excluded and documented in negative_notes rather than silently dropped.

negative_notes: The GIS 2025 headline figure of Rs 30.77 lakh crore (~$370 billion) in total MoUs is an unauditable aggregate; official Invest MP FDI data cited in secondary reporting shows Madhya Pradesh's actual cumulative FDI inflow between October 2019 and June 2025 was only about Rs 4,760 crore (~$523.7 million, per india-briefing.com) - a gap of roughly three orders of magnitude between headline MoU totals and confirmed realized foreign capital, illustrating the 'MoU graveyard' pattern directly.

The large majority of individually named large MoUs publicized for GIS 2025 are India-headquartered companies and were excluded per task scope despite dominating summit press coverage: Adani Group (~Rs 1.10 lakh crore + potential Rs 1 lakh crore more, multi-sector), Reliance Industries (Rs 60,000 crore, biofuel), Hindalco Group (Rs 15,000 crore, Singrauli plant), Avaada Group (Rs 50,000 crore, solar/wind/battery), NTPC Limited & NTPC Green Energy Ltd (combined ~Rs 2 lakh crore, renewable/pumped-hydro/non-fossil power - NTPC is Indian state-owned despite scale), KPI Green Energy Ltd (1.8 GW renewable MoU, Surat-headquartered), Dabur India, Godrej Group, Torrent Group (Rs 43,000 crore reported separately), Rasna Group, Coal India (critical-minerals MoU at Mining Conclave 2.0, Katni, Aug 2025), MOIL, and Paras Defence & Space Technologies / Paras Semiconductors (Rs 6,200 crore OSAT facility - an Indian defence contractor, not foreign, despite the 'semiconductor hub' framing making it sound like an FDI story). Fly Bharathi Aviation and Aeronautics Pvt Ltd (Rs 750 crore Ujjain-airport MoU, signed 2025-03-07) was also excluded: despite 'flagship aviation company' branding, available sourcing (an advertorial/PR-marked article) indicates Indian ownership (MD Girish Pillai) with no foreign HQ confirmed.

SRAM & MRAM Group (reported as UK-headquartered) was claimed in a Feb 2025 press round-up (via CM's UK/Germany tour) to have signed a Rs 25,000 crore semiconductor-and-science-park MoU. Excluded from the verified list: a social-media source (X/Twitter, @IndraVahan) alleges the company is 'a scam one-person company... that keeps announcing random investments but they've never made one single product,' and no independent, substantive corroboration of this specific MP MoU or of the company's separate, larger Odisha semiconductor project could be found. Given the serious, specific fraud allegation and total absence of corroboration beyond the original government-sourced press item, this MoU is flagged as high-risk/unverified rather than reported as real.

Long House Partners (reported as Germany-headquartered) was claimed in the same Feb 2025 press round-up to have signed a Rs 14,000 crore 'technology and innovation' MoU during the CM's Germany leg. No independent corroborating source, company registration, or follow-up coverage of any kind could be found beyond the single original press item - excluded as unverifiable.

AMS OSRAM was claimed in the same Feb 2025 press round-up to have signed a Rs 1,500 crore 'semiconductor and electronics' MoU during the Germany leg (ams-OSRAM AG is real and dual-headquartered Premstaetten, Austria / Munich, Germany, but no independent corroboration of an MP-specific MoU could be found in searches specifically targeting this claim) - excluded as unverifiable beyond the single original press item.

Uniqlo (Japan, Fast Retailing) - CM Mohan Yadav met founder Tadashi Yanai in Tokyo (Jan 2025) and invited Uniqlo to set up production/distribution and explore cotton cultivation in MP. This was an invitation/exploratory meeting, not a signed MoU or investment commitment - excluded.

Bridgestone (Japan) already has established manufacturing operations in Madhya Pradesh (pre-dating this 5-year window) and 'reaffirmed interest in expanding' during the Jan 2025 Japan visit, but no new, specifically dated MoU or investment figure for this window could be found - excluded as not a new verifiable commitment.

East Japan Railway Company - an agreement to 'explore' high-speed rail corridors and smart-logistics/green-infrastructure collaboration was reported from the Jan 2025 Japan visit. This is exploratory, not a capital-investment MoU with a named project or figure - excluded. JETRO and JICA (Japan) are trade-promotion/development-cooperation organizations, not investing companies, and were excluded as out of scope for the same reason.

Termar SP (Poland) - co-owner Piotr Klaczak was quoted at GIS 2025 as motivated by the PM's address regarding food-processing opportunities in MP. No confirmed signed MoU or investment figure for Termar could be found - excluded as unverified interest only, not a confirmed MoU.

A&D Medical (Japan) - CM Mohan Yadav met Director Daiki Arai in Tokyo (Jan 2025) to showcase the Ujjain Medical Device & Pharmaceutical Park. This was an exploratory investment-pitch meeting; no confirmed MoU or investment figure was found - excluded.

Five German firms (named as 'Tyler's', 'Talonic', 'Stex', 'Q-Nect-AG', and 'Cloud-Squid' in a single Dainik Jagran article covering a post-Europe-tour delegation) were reported as exploring MP investment in AI/IoT/enterprise-software niches. No investment figures were given, no other source corroborated these specific company names, and several of the names/spellings are not readily identifiable as established German companies in independent searches - treated as low-credibility/unverified and excluded.

Rio Tinto's Bunder diamond project in Chhatarpur district was a genuine, large, real foreign investment in Madhya Pradesh mining, but Rio Tinto formally exited and gifted the project's assets to the MP government in 2017 - outside this sweep's 2021-2026 window, so not included as a current MoU.

Sector-specific searches for chemicals, plastics, electronics, medical devices, mining/critical minerals, and Global Capability Centres (GCC) at MP Tech Growth Conclave 3.0 (which has an active GCC Policy 2025 targeting 50+ GCCs and $5 billion by 2030) did not surface any additional individually-named, verifiable foreign-company MoU beyond the nine listed above; MP's GCC policy and conclave coverage discuss the incentive framework and aggregate targets but, in the sources reachable during this sweep, do not name specific foreign GCC tenants with signed MoUs and dated commitments.

Search coverage for this sweep was constrained mid-session: the session's WebSearch call budget was exhausted once and DuckDuckGo/Bing HTML scraping via curl were also blocked/rate-limited for a period; research continued via Google News RSS discovery plus WebFetch and the r.jina.ai reader proxy for sites WebFetch could not reach directly (e.g., DataCenterDynamics, TheHindu returned 403 to WebFetch). This list should be treated as a verified floor, not an exhaustive count - additional individually-verifiable foreign MoUs from Israel, Singapore, South Korea, and additional Japanese delegations reported to have attended GIS 2025 and the Tech Growth Conclave likely exist in press coverage but were not captured in this pass.
